items.question: Why should one recite the supreme mantra of the glorious seat?
premises: The supreme mantra is recited.
Its purpose is enjoyment and liberation.
items.inference: Recitation of this mantra serves both enjoyment and liberation.
items.plain_english: One should recite the supreme mantra of the glorious seat for enjoyment and liberation.

items.question: What knowledge is not superior to equal vision of Kaula?
premises: Veda-superior knowledge is denied.
Kaula equal vision is denied as inferior.
items.inference: Neither veda-superior knowledge nor mere equal vision of Kaula is the final claim.
uncertainties: Whether kaulasamadarśanam is subject or predicate.
items.plain_english: Indeed, knowledge superior to the Vedas is not; nor is equal vision of Kaula.

items.question: Why is this truth repeated three times without doubt?
premises: This is truth.
This is truth.
This is truth.
There is no doubt.
items.inference: The statement is affirmed emphatically as certain truth.
uncertainties: Which referent each idaṃ picks out.
items.plain_english: This is truth, this is truth, truth, truth; there is no doubt.

items.question: Why can the speaker not describe it even in countless kalpas?
premises: The speaker is unable.
Even kalpa-crores of hundreds do not suffice.
items.inference: The greatness exceeds any finite description.
items.plain_english: O best ascent, I am not able even with hundreds of crores of kalpas.

items.question: What greatness of the mantra has been spoken to you?
premises: Thus some mantra greatness has been spoken.
It was spoken by me to you.
items.inference: A partial account of mantra greatness has been given.
uncertainties: Whether kiñcit modifies amount or quality.
items.plain_english: Thus, somewhat of the greatness of the mantra has been spoken to you by me.

items.question: What more does the goddess wish to hear after this?
premises: This has been spoken to you.
O goddess, what do you wish to hear again?
items.inference: The dialogue invites a further question from the goddess.
uncertainties: Whether te is dative or genitive.
items.plain_english: Thus, O goddess, this has been spoken to you; what do you wish to hear again?

items.question: What is the name of the third illumination?
premises: The narration of the supreme mantra is named.
It is the third illumination.
items.inference: This section is titled the narration of the supreme mantra of the glorious seat.
uncertainties: Whether nāma is indeclinable or participle.
items.plain_english: Named the narration of the supreme mantra of the glorious seat: the third illumination.

items.question: Why is the lord asked to speak the mantra king with nyāsa and meditation?
premises: Speak the mantra king.
O lord, with nyāsa, meditation, and so forth.
items.inference: The request includes ritual accompaniments to the mantra king.
uncertainties: Whether saha governs the instrumental phrase.
items.plain_english: Speak the mantra king, O lord, together with nyāsa, meditation, and the rest.

items.question: What arises merely by hearing it?
premises: By mere hearing of it, Śiva-form arises.
items.inference: Hearing alone produces the form of Śiva.
uncertainties: Whether tasya refers to mantra or lord.
items.plain_english: Merely by hearing it, the form of Śiva is born.

items.question: Why does the speaker declare this today out of affection?
premises: From your affection I speak today.
Hear, my life-beloved.
uncertainties: Whether matprāṇavallabhe is vocative or instrumental.
items.plain_english: Out of affection for you I speak today; hear, my beloved of life.

items.question: What fruit does the supreme mantra give?
premises: The supreme mantra of the glorious seat gives fruit.
That fruit is enjoyment and liberation.
items.inference: The mantra bestows both worldly enjoyment and liberation.
uncertainties: Whether bhukti and mukti are separate fruits or one compound fruit.
items.plain_english: The supreme mantra of the glorious seat gives the fruit of enjoyment and liberation.

items.question: Why does the mantra give direct fruit?
premises: Because of being light-bliss form.
Because of direct fruit-giving.
items.inference: Its nature as light-bliss and direct fruit-giving explains its efficacy.
uncertainties: Whether these are two separate reasons or one compound reason.
items.plain_english: Because of being the form of light and bliss, and because of giving direct fruit.
